title: India's Sonam Maskar and Himanshu Dhillon Win Bronze at ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou
excerpt: The Indian duo combined for 441.2 points in the 10m air rifle mixed team final, securing India's latest podium finish as the country wraps up a four-medal campaign in China.
body:
• Sonam Uttam Maskar and Himanshu Dhillon won bronze in the 10m air rifle mixed team event at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou, China, finishing behind two Chinese pairs.
  • Himanshu Dhillon, making his first senior World Cup final appearance, scored 220.6 alongside Sonam's 220.6 for a combined 441.2 in the final.
  • India's second pair, Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Rakesh Mane, narrowly missed a medal by finishing fourth with 378.8 points.
  • India concluded their Hangzhou World Cup campaign with four medals overall, building momentum ahead of the Asian Games and World Championships.

Indian rifle shooters Sonam Uttam Maskar and Himanshu Dhillon clinched the bronze medal in the 10m air rifle mixed team event at the ISSF World Cup in Hangzhou on Monday, adding another podium finish to India's growing reputation in international shooting.

The pair delivered consistent performances across both qualification and finals, combining for 634.6 in qualification — Sonam contributing 317.2 and Himanshu 317.4 — before scoring 441.2 in the medal round. China's top two pairs swept gold and silver, with Wang Zifei and Sheng Lihao taking the top spot and Du Yuchen and Zhang Changhong claiming second.

Himanshu's Breakthrough on the Senior Stage

For Himanshu Dhillon, the bronze carries particular significance. The young shooter was making his first appearance in a senior ISSF World Cup final, having previously competed extensively in junior events.

"It was a great experience competing in my first senior World Cup final. I believed in myself, trusted my coach's guidance and relied on my strengths. Winning my first senior World Cup medal makes this achievement very special."

— Himanshu Dhillon, Indian shooter

Sonam, meanwhile, continues to build on a strong 2024 season that included silver medals at the ISSF World Cup in Cairo and the ISSF World Cup Final in New Delhi, along with a fifth-place finish in Granada earlier this year.

India's Second Pair Falls Just Short

India had both mixed team pairs qualify for the final — a testament to the depth of talent in the country's rifle shooting programme. Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Rakesh Mane advanced with a combined qualification score of 634.2 but could not sustain their form in the medal round, finishing fourth with 378.8 points. Elavenil scored 190.5 while Parth contributed 188.3.

The near-miss echoed a familiar pattern for India at Hangzhou. Earlier in the competition, Sonam and Elavenil both reached the women's individual 10m air rifle final but faded in the later stages — Sonam finishing fifth with 187.7 and Elavenil sixth with 166.9 — as China continued to dominate the medal table.

A Strong Campaign Heading Into a Pivotal Season

The bronze capped a four-medal campaign for India at the Hangzhou leg, their best return of the 2026 ISSF World Cup season. With stages in Cairo and the World Cup Final in Rome still to come, the performance signals India's rifle and pistol shooters are rounding into form during a year loaded with high-stakes competitions.

"Winning a medal is always important because it gives us confidence for the assignments ahead. Experience matters more than anything, and this performance will motivate us as we prepare for the Asian Games and the World Championships later this season."

— Sonam Uttam Maskar, Indian shooter

What It Means for the Diaspora

India's shooting programme has become one of the country's most reliable medal producers on the global stage, a development closely followed by the Indian diaspora. Sonam's rise, in particular, represents a new generation of Indian women athletes building careers in precision sports that once received little domestic attention. For diaspora communities watching the Asian Games approach, the Hangzhou results suggest India's shooters will once again be serious contenders.

What's Next

The ISSF World Cup season continues with the fourth stage in Cairo later this year, followed by the World Cup Final in Rome. Both events will serve as critical preparation for the Asian Games, where India will look to convert consistent World Cup form into continental gold medals. With Sonam and Himanshu demonstrating chemistry in the mixed team format and India's bench depth evident from having two pairs in the final, the programme appears well-positioned for the competitions ahead.
